From week 12 on in 2024 (final seven games) Bucky Irving averaged 18.3 fantasy points per game and about 120 total yards per game as a top-10 RB; he is Sal's 41st overall player.

DK Metcalf has 19 targets (25% target share, top five in the NFL) and is third in the NFL in routes run at 88 (44 per week), with 2 registered drops; Aaron Rodgers has the third-most pass attempts in the NFL. Metcalf's two-week line: 4 catches for 40 yards on 10 targets, with games of 8 and 6.7 PPR points.

Javonte Williams through two weeks: over 80% of snaps in week 2, 76% of snaps and 71% of rush attempts overall; game logs of 12 carries for 41 yards and 12 for 30, saved in week 1 by a receiving touchdown.

Javonte Williams is averaging 2.96 yards per carry, 50% of his runs have gone for two or fewer yards, and he is 42nd of 43 running backs in first downs with two on 24 carries; Dallas's offensive line is dead last in yards before contact.
Dallas Pro Bowl lineman Tyler Smith is on IR with week 5 as his earliest and targeted return.

Bryce Young is the QB2 in fantasy football with three touchdowns in each of the last two weeks and only one interception; his week-1 high was 31 fantasy points on 361 passing yards against Chicago. He is at 8.9 yards per attempt and a 10.5 average depth of target, blowing away his career averages.
Carolina is playing the fastest of any team in the NFL at 23 seconds per play and ranks number one in neutral pass rate.
Bryce Young's cautionary precedent: last year in Atlanta he threw for 448 yards and three touchdowns, then followed with passing totals of 169, 206, 163, 191 and 54 yards.

Patrick Mahomes' fantasy QB finishes: QB1, QB4, QB4 pre-Nagy, then QB8, QB11, QB11 during the Matt Nagy years. This season he has six touchdowns through two weeks (one rushing and two passing in week 1 on 27 attempts for 184 yards and 20+ points, three passing in week 2 on 47 attempts).
Atlanta is the fourth team since 1978 to go its first two games without running a single play in the red zone.
In the games Drake London played with Michael Penix last year he was on pace for 180 targets and finished as the WR5 (WR1 on a week); Bijan Robinson was on pace for over 100 targets with Penix.

Vegas for Thursday Night Football: Green Bay -5.5 over Atlanta with a 43.5 total at Lambeau Field. Bills are favored by 7 over the Chargers. Bengals-Steelers in Pittsburgh has a 42.5 total, and the Carolina game also has a 42.5 total.

The Chargers are 30th in EPA per play, 30th in percentage of drives resulting in a score and 31st in turnover differential, having lost back-to-back home games 26-14; they are only the second team ever to lose consecutive home games by double digits to teams with a sub-.200 win percentage the prior year (the other: the 1926 Racine Tornadoes).
The Raiders currently rank as the number one fantasy defense through two weeks.
The last time Joe Burrow played in Pittsburgh he finished as the QB18 with one touchdown.

Green Bay's backfield: Chris Brooks leads in snaps (trusted in pass protection) and went 4 carries for 11 yards last game; both Kaleb Johnson and Marshawn Lloyd fumbled, with Johnson recovering his; Lloyd scored a receiving touchdown. A.J. Dillon had three carries for negative total yards.
Green Bay had four offensive linemen leave the week 2 game injured and internally discussed using Tucker Kraft at an offensive line position (per Graziano); one tackle went to IR.
FAAB results in the Footballers' league of record: Derrick Henry 4.65 (next-highest bid 4.51), Jeremiyah Love 3.34, Quinshon Judkins 1.56, Mike Evans 1.21.
Their league of record uses median scoring: each team plays its head-to-head opponent and also the league median that week, so up to two wins per week are available.

Excluding kneel-downs, sacks, scrambles and throwaways — plays on which skill players can't score fantasy points — the Dolphins are averaging only 46.5 plays per game, the worst full-season mark in the Fantasy Points database era; the historically bad 2025 Raiders ran about 50.
Miami is bottom-three in the NFL in yards per game through two weeks.
Defenses load the box against De'Von Achane at the third-highest rate in the NFL: 36% of his carries face a stacked front with at least one extra man.
De'Von Achane's Week 2: 20-24 carries for 74 yards (3.7 yards per carry) plus 3 catches for 19 yards, and he has not scored a touchdown yet this season.

Miami's pass-catching corps is Malik Washington (slot), rookie Caleb Douglas (foot/ankle injury, in a cast per Sal, not practicing), rookies Chris Bell and Kevin Coleman, and TE Greg Dulcich; Miami also has a defensive-minded head coach.
Kirk Cousins has more rushing attempts on the season than Malik Willis; Willis had 6 rushes for 39 yards in Week 1 and almost nothing since.

Sal's rest-of-season ordinal: De'Von Achane 30th overall, D'Andre Swift 31st, Malik Nabers 32nd, TreVeyon Henderson 61st, Josh Downs ~65th (92nd before the update), Brock Purdy 68th, Aaron Jones 93rd; Drake London 21st, George Pickens 23rd, Bijan Robinson 2nd.

Aaron Jones is about to turn 32; in Week 2 he played 80% of snaps and took 85% of the rush attempts for 23 carries, 105 rushing yards and only 10.5 fantasy points with no receiving role. Week 1 was a split: Jordan Mason 15 carries to Jones' 12.

Kevin O'Connell said Aaron Jones was sore after shouldering the Week-2 workload, and indicated Jordan Mason will be on IR about three more weeks with a fractured finger/thumb; Minnesota signed DeeJay Dallas to the active roster midweek.

Rookie Demond Claiborne played only 4% of Minnesota's snaps in Week 2 and weighs well under 200 pounds; Minnesota was down to its backup quarterback with Kyler Murray already hurt, which raised the pass-protection bar.
Aaron Jones did not practice Wednesday, then was limited Thursday (an upgrade).
TreVeyon Henderson's Week 2 debut: 16 carries for 76 yards with a 39-yard touchdown, 60% of snaps and 67% of rush attempts; excluding the long touchdown he averaged 2.7 yards per carry.

Rhamondre Stevenson played only 36% of snaps in Week 2 after an early fumble; per Ryan Heath, from that fumble to the two-minute warning the split was Henderson 76% of snaps to Stevenson 24%. Stevenson has 18 fumbles since the start of 2021, more than any other player.

Chuba Hubbard is playing 66% of Carolina's snaps and is RB8 at 17.8-19.1 fantasy points per game; Jonathon Brooks is on IR and the only other backs are A.J. Dillon and possibly Trevor Etienne if elevated. Carolina did not sign Austin Ekeler.
Only five running backs have finished top-12 in both of the first two weeks: Kenneth Walker III, Jahmyr Gibbs, Derrick Henry, Jonathan Taylor and Chuba Hubbard.
Jalen Coker leads Carolina with a 29% target share and averages 102 yards per game; Tetairoa McMillan has a 27% target share, averages 88 yards per game and has only a 59% catch rate.

Bryce Young is tied for the NFL lead with 6 passing touchdowns, has thrown 73 passes (6th-most in the league, inflated by trailing big in Week 1) and is averaging 9.8 yards per attempt against a 6.3 YPA baseline over his past two seasons; Carolina is tied for 4th in total yards per game with Baltimore.

Carolina's two opponents were the Bears (possibly a historically bad defense given preseason injuries) and the Falcons, one of the most blitz-heavy teams through two weeks with no pass rush — Aaron Rodgers also looked great against Atlanta in Week 1.
Dave Canales handed the Panthers' play-calling duties to Brad Idzik.

Stefon Diggs (32, nearly 33) leads Washington with a 24% target share while running only 60% of the routes, and leads the team by over 10 percentage points with a 31% targets-per-route-run rate; he is a top-10 fantasy WR at 16.5 points and 7.5 targets per game.
Terry McLaurin has the worst catchable-target rate in the NFL at 54%; he had a touchdown called back and a 15-20-yard catch over the middle called back in Week 2 before Jayden Daniels got hurt.
In Marcus Mariota's five starts last season, Terry McLaurin averaged 3.53 yards per route run and 14.3 fantasy points per game, finishing as WR14 over that stretch.
Marcus Mariota started eight games last season averaging 11 fantasy points, with a 23.3-point game against Denver.

Denzel Boston leads Cleveland with a 22% target share; first-round pick KC Concepcion is at 20% and Harold Fannin Jr. at 17%. Boston's production is two long touchdowns: a 46-yarder in Week 1 and a 55-yarder in Week 2 after three Buccaneers defenders missed tackles (5 catches, 95 yards on the day).

Deshaun Watson's Week 2 (24 of 30, 238 yards, 7.9 yards per attempt, 2 TDs, 80% completion) was his best game in six years with Cleveland — against a Tampa Bay defense that missed three tackles on one play.

Per Scott Barrett's targets-per-route-run and separation chart of WRs with 10-plus targets, Rashee Rice ranks at the very bottom — below Chris Godwin, Cooper Kupp and Dyami Brown — while JSN, Ladd McConkey, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Garrett Wilson, Stefon Diggs and Mike Evans grade out well.
Rashee Rice has been targeted on only 11% of his routes.

Malik Nabers was around Sal's 17th-ranked rest-of-season player heading into Week 2 with a 32% target share before re-injuring his shoulder; he fully participated in Wednesday practice and X-rays came back clean.

Jameis Winston was 11 of 27 last week (near a 30% completion rate); the Giants-Titans game has the lowest over/under of the week at 38.5 with the Giants -3, a 68% chance of rain and potentially high winds.
Cam Skattebo has seen 16 and 18 opportunities in the first two weeks as the Giants' lead back.
Matthew Golden and Christian Watson are tied for the Green Bay team-high 27% target share; Golden's Week-2 box score is understated because he drew two personal fouls.

With A.J. Terrell out for Atlanta, Matthew Golden draws mostly Mike Hughes, who ranks 89th of 128 qualifying coverage players at 1.4 yards allowed per coverage snap — the best individual matchup on the Thursday slate per Sal's matchups tool.

Tucker Kraft ran 84% of Green Bay's routes in Week 2 after about 40% in Week 1, and played 98% of snaps; Atlanta is 29th in schedule-adjusted points allowed to tight ends and already gave up production to Pat Freiermuth and Darren Waller.
Green Bay right tackle Zach Tom is out, adding to the Packers' offensive-line problems; Jayden Reed is out for Thursday.
Travis Kelce leads the Chiefs with a 25% target share, leads all NFL pass catchers in yards after the catch and leads the team in targets per route run; he is 36 and turns 37 within weeks.

Kansas City is a 10.5-point road favorite at Miami with a 46.5 total and a 28.5-point implied team total, the second-highest of the season; the Chiefs are 28-3 as double-digit favorites but have failed to cover in 55% of those games.

Brock Purdy leads all quarterbacks in EPA per play and is at an 8.9% touchdown rate (his sustainable baseline is about 7%); San Francisco is an 8.5-point home favorite against Arizona, missing Stribling, Demarcus Robinson and Christian Kirk, and possibly Mike Evans.
Deebo Samuel's alignment split is 50% out wide, 45% in the slot and 5% in the backfield.

Jared Goff threw for 327 yards and 4 touchdowns last week; he has averaged 21 fantasy points per game at home since 2022 and Detroit has the fifth-highest implied team total this week (Lions -6.5, total 47.5). The over has hit in each of Detroit's last six games.

Tyler Shough is the first player in NFL history with 3,000 passing yards and a 67% completion rate through his first 13 career games; Kellen Moore's pace gives the offense roughly five extra drop-backs — about an extra drive — per game.
Indianapolis is 30th in EPA per rush attempt and 31st in yards per carry allowed; David Montgomery had only 8 opportunities for under 5 fantasy points last week yet still out-snapped Woody Marks.

Denver is dead last in EPA per rush and dead last in yards after contact per attempt allowed, and 29th in fantasy points allowed to running backs; Blake Corum is averaging 6.0 yards per carry on 22 attempts, second only to Kenneth Walker III.

Buffalo's defense is 31st in points per drive allowed, 28th in pass success rate allowed and 30th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers, leaking specifically to slot receivers; the Chargers-Bills line is Buffalo -7 with a 50.5 total, the second-highest of the week.

Ladd McConkey barely practiced last week and played under half the snaps as a decoy; he was a full participant on Wednesday this week. The Chargers' offense posted -0.41 EPA per play without him and +0.12 with him (cited previously), and looked significantly better with him in the first half against Arizona.

Josh Downs had 9 targets for 7 catches and 72 yards last week, holds a 30% first-read target share and 29% of the Colts' receiving yards, and averages over 10 fantasy points per game in five career games against Houston; Alec Pierce is out of the picture for at least six weeks.
Dalton Schultz went 12 catches on 14 targets for 140 yards against Cincinnati last week; Cincinnati has been the tight-end funnel to target for roughly eight straight years.

Tyler Warren led all NFL pass catchers in yards after the catch through the first three weeks of last season; his yards after catch per reception has fallen from 10.8 to 3.8, and his fantasy value is currently propped up entirely by touchdowns on about 30 receiving yards.

Dalton Kincaid was the 25th overall pick and played roughly 38% of snaps last year through a knee injury; he is now healthy, running far more routes, and has always been excellent on a per-route basis.
Harold Fannin Jr. has a 17% target share through two weeks.
Carolina is dead last in yards per carry allowed, rushing touchdowns allowed and EPA per rush this season; they were also bad last year and one of the worst run defenses of all time the year before.

Carnell Tate has a 24% target share as a rookie but has not seen a single target 20-plus yards downfield all season; Tennessee's touch distribution went 7 carries for Tony Pollard in Week 1 to 14 in Week 2, and Pollard is averaging 4.7 yards per carry.
Detroit is top-five in the league in pace of play but the Jets are so slow that the combined game pace ranks bottom-five (per Jared Smola's matchup pace data).
The Aidan Hutchinson-led Lions have the highest pressure rate in the NFL; Geno Smith's Jets have yet to commit a turnover this season.
Jameson Williams played 97% of snaps last week; Isaac TeSlaa had one more target than Williams in that game.
Adonai Mitchell is ahead of Garrett Wilson in target share.

Through two weeks Pittsburgh's defense ranks first against quarterbacks, second against wide receivers and fifth against tight ends — with the caveat that its two opponents were Cooper Rush and a struggling Drake Maye; Cincinnati is -3.5 in Pittsburgh with a 42.5 total.
Houston is -2.5 against Indianapolis with a 42.5 total; both teams are 0-2.
Carolina is -2.5 at Cleveland with a 42.5 total; Myles Garrett is no longer on the Browns.
Seattle-Washington has a 40.5 total with Seattle implied for 24 points and Washington implied for 16.8 — the lowest implied team total of the week.
The Ravens-Cowboys game carries a 52.5-point total, the biggest of the Sunday slate; it is an international game played in Brazil.
A.J. Brown's injury is a high ankle sprain that nearly required surgery, with a six-to-eight-week recovery re-reported Thursday; Sal expects five to seven more missed weeks plus a ramp-up.

Jayden Daniels' injury involves ligaments that were already torn and were not repaired; if he has surgery his season is over, and if he doesn't it is four to six weeks in a brace with a high re-injury rate. Kurt Warner said publicly he suffered the same injury in 2007 and played the next week.
Josh Jacobs is on the commissioner's exempt list facing a possible four-to-six-game suspension, with the games he has already missed counting toward it; he dealt with a groin injury in camp.
Keenan Allen's three-game suspension has been pushed, likely until after court proceedings, which probably means after the season.

Sean McVay said publicly that Puka Nacua is 'not making great progress' but that it is not a hernia and not a torn ACL; Nacua did not practice Wednesday or Thursday and has all the symptoms of a core-muscle injury without that diagnosis — surgery would mean six-plus additional weeks.
Terrance Ferguson posted 9 targets, 6 catches for 54 yards and a touchdown on 36 of 62 snaps with Nacua inactive, and Stafford threw for 327 and 4.
Davante Adams is nearly 34 years old and is Sal's WR4 for Week 3 with Nacua out.

Zay Flowers did not practice Wednesday or Thursday with a hamstring but is traveling to Brazil; the last Brazil game (Packers-Eagles) had a surface where defenders could get no grip, which is why Baltimore may protect him.

Sal's Week 3 wide receiver ranks: Christian Watson WR10, Matthew Golden WR17, Mike Evans WR22, an if-active Zay Flowers ~WR25, Xavier Worthy WR30, Adonai Mitchell WR32, with Jaylen Waddle and Ladd McConkey back-to-back.

Sal's Week 3 tight end projections: Dalton Schultz TE7 at 12.2 points, Oronde Gadsden II TE20 at 8.2, Kyle Pitts TE21 at 8.0; Travis Kelce is his TE2 and Mark Andrews would be a top-three TE if Zay Flowers is out.
Sal's start-sit tool projects Jaylen Warren 14.7 points and Aaron Jones 12.7 for Week 3, pending Rico Dowdle's status.
Jonah Coleman did not participate in Wednesday's practice while J.K. Dobbins and R.J. Harvey were limited participants; Coleman left the Week-2 game with an ankle issue but returned and scored.
Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears both missed Wednesday practice with ankle injuries; Pollard was upgraded to limited participant Thursday.

Brock Bowers was a limited participant Wednesday and again Thursday; Travis Etienne Jr. was limited with a hamstring despite getting no work; Mike Evans and Keon Coleman did not practice Wednesday; DJ Moore was limited Wednesday but did not practice Thursday; Michael Pittman Jr. was limited and still injured; Nico Collins did not practice.

Saquon Barkley is officially limited with a stinger and is unlikely to play in Week 3; Caleb Williams is not expected to play Week 3 and Sal doubts he plays Week 4, which could leave Chicago starting a third-string quarterback against the Eagles' defensive line on Monday night.
DeVonta Smith did not practice with a hamstring — the same hamstring that cost him three weeks of training camp — though it may be a veteran rest day after a Monday night game.
Giants left tackle Andrew Thomas was downgraded on the injury report.
Mason Taylor did not practice and looks out for the Jets, opening the tight-end role for first-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq, whose PrizePicks receiving line is 25.5 yards.
David Njoku and Charlie Kolar are both on IR for the Chargers, which forces Oronde Gadsden II onto the field on nearly every play; the Chargers had been running a slow, tight-end-heavy scheme.
Darren Waller and Tetairoa McMillan carry identical 59.5-yard PrizePicks receiving projections this week; Waller's snap counts are currently very low.
Rico Dowdle still has not practiced for Pittsburgh while Jaylen Warren returned as a limited participant; DK Metcalf is listed as limited.

Michael Penix Jr. was medically cleared over a week ago but said he wasn't ready; Atlanta had acquired Tua Tagovailoa in the offseason specifically to replace him, and Tua looked worse than Penix in preseason.
Jaxson Dart is done for the season, making Jameis Winston the Giants' starter.
Patrick Mahomes' QB finishes were 1, 4, 4, 1 before Matt Nagy called the offense and 8, 11, 11 during the Nagy years; Nagy is now gone.

Sal says a fully participating practice report outweighs injury speculation: he acted on the Nabers 'fully participates' tweet plus clean X-rays rather than the pessimistic reads circulating on Twitter.

Sal's rest-of-season ordinal has Jahmyr Gibbs first, Bijan Robinson second, then Jonathan Taylor and Kenneth Walker III, with Ja'Marr Chase around fifth, Derrick Henry around 12th, Drake London 21st, George Pickens 23rd and Ashton Jeanty inside the top 15.

Both channels place Mike McDaniel as the coach controlling Oronde Gadsden II's usage on the Chargers, and both note Miami now has a defensive-minded head coach with Achane on pace for more targets since McDaniel left.
Jalen Ramsey missed Wednesday practice but was participating Thursday, which Andy called the swing factor for the Steelers' defensive matchup with Cincinnati.

Sal is publishing six YouTube videos a week this season, including a Saturday 11am news dump built off Friday practice reports, plus live streams Sunday, Monday and Thursday before kickoff that he unlists afterwards.
